text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Hosni Mubarak visits Toshka today to inspect work on the South Valley Development Project. The soil analysis studies have been encouraging.

- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri says in Tunis that the law on investment incentives will come out this month. Investors will be able to start their projects immediately without administrative approvals.
- Mubarak met Sir Peter de la Billiere, a director of Flemings, who described his talks as constructive.
- U.S. Vice President Al Gore will visit Egypt in May to sign a new partnership agreement.
- Ganzouri said in Tunis that all projects in the New Valley will be exempt from the approvals procedure.
- Sir Peter de la Billiere said after meeting Mubarak that Flemings would open a branch in Egypt to take part in investing.

- Ismail Osman, the chairman of Arab Contractors, said there is a move towards selling the company as part of the privatisation programme. He said privatisation of the company was being studied in depth because the company is one of the biggest contractors in the Middle East and because the company cannot be broken up and sold off in pieces.
- Private-sector investors have decided to set up seven new cement factories with a production capacity of eight million tonnes a year.
- The rain and thunder storm on Sunday took the weather forecasters by surprise.
- The names of the ruling National Democratic Party's candidates for local elections will be announced tomorrow.
